steps.instruction: Add a public method clearWatched(): void that removes every item whose `watched` flag is true, in one operation. After it runs: items() holds only the unwatched items, in their previous relative order; watchedCount() is 0; count() equals the number of remaining items. Persist the updated list exactly the way add/remove/toggleWatched do, so a WatchlistStore instance created afterwards (for example after a page reload) loads the already-cleared list. Calling it when no item is watched must leave the list unchanged. Add spec coverage for clearWatched in your own spec file, in the style of your existing tests; do not change or remove any existing test.

Add a Clear watched button to the watchlist view that removes every movie whose `watched` flag is true in one click. The WatchlistStore you import is gaining a new method in this same round; you will receive clearWatched(): void on the store — it removes all watched items (unwatched items keep their order), keeps items/count/watchedCount consistent, and persists the change. Add a public component method clearWatched(): void that (capturing watchedCount() before clearing if you want the number for the message) delegates to store.clearWatched() and then sets `announcement` to a non-empty screen-reader message about what was cleared, following the same pattern as your existing remove method. In watchlist.html add a button that: shows the visible text 'Clear watched' (so that text is also its accessible name); is always rendered together with the other watchlist controls regardless of state (do not hide it with structural directives); binds the `disabled` attribute so it is disabled exactly when watchedCount() === 0; and invokes the component's clearWatched() on click. Place it near the watched-count/progress summary and style it consistently with the existing buttons (watchlist.scss may be extended). Do not change the behaviour of existing rows, existing buttons, or the single-item remove announcement. Add spec coverage for the new button and component method in your own spec file; do not change or remove any existing test.

input.reason: tsc is clean and 42/43 tests pass; the only failure is my acceptance test pinning persistence: after clearWatched(), a freshly constructed WatchlistStore loads an empty list even though unwatched movies remained. In-memory behaviour of clearWatched is correct (the other acceptance tests pass), so the bug is purely in what clearWatched writes to storage — the entry ends up empty/removed instead of holding the remaining items. steps.instruction:
Fix the persistence behaviour of clearWatched(). The current implementation updates the in-memory list correctly, but it corrupts the persisted state: after calling clearWatched() on a store containing both watched and unwatched movies, a newly constructed WatchlistStore loads an empty list instead of the remaining unwatched movies — the storage entry the store uses ends up emptied or removed rather than holding the remaining items.

Required behaviour: clearWatched() must leave storage in exactly the state your other mutators would leave it in. After it runs, the storage entry must contain precisely the remaining unwatched items, in their previous relative order, so a WatchlistStore constructed afterwards (for example after a page reload) loads that already-cleared list. Concretely: do not remove or clear the storage key, do not write an empty list while unwatched items remain, and do not write the removed/watched items. If nothing was watched, the persisted list stays unchanged.

Implementation guidance: reuse the exact same persistence code path (same key, same serialization) that add(), remove() and toggleWatched() already use, invoked after the in-memory list is updated — or equivalently, delete the watched items one by one through the existing remove(), which already persists. Either way, a second WatchlistStore instance constructed in the same JS realm after clearWatched() must report items() equal to the remaining unwatched items, watchedCount() === 0, and count() equal to the remaining length.

Add a test to your own spec file, in the style of your existing tests, that: adds one watched and one unwatched movie, calls clearWatched(), constructs a new WatchlistStore, and asserts the new instance loads only the unwatched movie. Do not change or remove any existing test.

content.text: The bug: persistence was only performed by a constructor `effect()`, which flushes asynchronously — so a `WatchlistStore` constructed right after `clearWatched()` reads a not-yet-updated (empty) storage entry, and its own effect later writes that empty list back. The fix is to persist synchronously through one shared code path (same key, same serialization) invoked by every mutator after the in-memory update.
